about: Split view's fluidity budgets (SPLIT-LEAD, 20 Oct 2026; release-1010/design/split/ANALYSIS.md): a pane carried by its bar across the page and a seam dragged, two docs beside Home, on a production build against the fake server side (surfaces.mjs --only split --device desktop), on a computer at 1x and at 4x (split view isn't on a phone). The row is fluid-21, Views side by side.

A drag holds 60 frames a second: frame p95 at most one refresh and at most 5% of frames dropped, as every drag in the app does. At 60 Hz a frame on time reads 16.7 or 16.8 ms here (timer jitter; a late one reads 33+), so a frame max of 16.8 is one refresh (FLUIDITY-LEAD, 21 Oct). The pane drag runs no layout per move (the ghost and the drop line move on transforms; the views take no pointer while one is carried); a seam's move changes a flex-grow, so its layouts are expected and its budget is frame time.

measured is the median of 5 runs on split-arrange-2026-10-20-fe c71c7ee33's build, heavy.sh --pcore on CPUs 0-7, next start on 24-29 (SPLIT-LEAD-2). At 1x (20 Oct 21:33): load 10 to 13, no busy run, every budget met. At 4x (21 Oct 04:24): load 16.5 to 17.3, every run just over the busy line; the 4x maxes are those runs' worst, and their targets are 1x's: neither drag holds 60 frames a second at 4x yet (fluid-21 stays short of WIN until they do).
Never raise a max to make a run pass. Lower it when a package brings a metric down.

splitPaneDragFrameP95Ms.source: A pane carried by its bar to the page's left: 60 moves 16 ms apart, then the drop and its settle. Every drag in the app holds 60 frames a second.

splitPaneDragDroppedPct.source: The same carry: frames dropped, at most 5%.

splitPaneDragLayouts.source: Layouts over the carry, the drop and its settle (the renderer's LayoutCount). 216 on the first run (busy); 175 once the views took no pointer during a carry. Target: the drop and its settle only, no layout per move (ANALYSIS §6); @dnd-kit's measuring still lays out on the way.

splitSeamDragFrameP95Ms.source: The seam between the first two views dragged 180 px right, then 360 px left: react-resizable-panels changes a flex-grow, so each move lays the views out; its budget is frame time.

splitSeamDragDroppedPct.source: The same seam drag: frames dropped, at most 5%.
